summary.short: Ley 27.742 declares a one-year public emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters and delegates listed powers to the executive. Title VII creates the RIGI investment incentive regime for large projects in listed sectors, open for two years from entry into force.
summary.long: Ley 27.742 declares a one-year public emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters and delegates listed powers to the executive. It reorganises state bodies and companies, privatises named state firms, amends administrative procedure (Law 19.549), public and private employment rules, concession rules, and hydrocarbon, gas and electricity regimes, including export authorisations, royalties and a unified energy regulator. Title VII creates the RIGI investment incentive regime for single-project vehicles in listed sectors: minimum computable investment of USD 200 million (sector amounts up to USD 900 million), a 40% investment condition for the first two years, local supplier commitments, and approval by the enforcement authority within 45 days. Approved projects receive 30-year stability guarantees; adhesion is open for two years from entry into force, extendable once by one year. Only part 1 of 2 was supplied (through Art. 179); this annotation covers that portion.
